claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: The moreover clauses are correctly scoped to an FVS S. If G-S has a cycle, a shortest such cycle is chordless and hence induced in G. Bipartiteness makes its length even, and an induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices; therefore the cycle has length 4, 6, or 8. This proves both directions of the hitting equivalence. Each component of G-S is a tree. A tree of diameter at least 7 has an induced path on eight vertices, so every component has diameter at most 6 and radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal and x is in S, then G-(S minus {x}) contains a cycle; since G-S is a forest, that cycle uses x and a path between two distinct neighbors of x in one component of G-S.
claims.search_method: Direct graph-theoretic proof, including checks of the shortest-cycle argument, induced-path length, and the inclusion-minimality quantifier.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: Enumerating all 4-, 6-, and 8-vertex subsets yields in O(n^8) time the rank-at-most-eight hypergraph of induced short cycles. By claim 0, its transversals are exactly the feedback vertex sets. Branching on every vertex of an unhit hyperedge gives T(k) at most 8T(k-1) plus O(n^8), hence O(8^k n^8), and is exhaustive because every solution must hit that edge. For approximation, greedily form a maximal vertex-disjoint family of p listed cycles and return their union U. Maximality means U hits every listed cycle and is therefore an FVS; vertex-disjointness gives OPT at least p, while |U| is at most 8p.
claims.search_method: Independent hitting-set reduction, branching recurrence analysis, and packing-versus-transversal approximation proof.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: An independent exhaustive checker introduced vertices in the fixed order of a required Hamilton path. Bipartiteness forces each possible edge to join opposite index parities, so enumerating every allowable earlier-neighbor subset is exhaustive. Integer-bit-mask predicates for C4 and induced P8 were each cross-checked by two independent tests. The numbers of admissible ordered graphs for q=1 through 15 were 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0. Thus no C4-free P8-free bipartite graph contains a simple 15-vertex path. In an undirected DFS forest, every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints and every root-to-leaf path consequently has at most 14 vertices. The bag containing each DFS vertex and all its ancestors is therefore a tree decomposition of width at most 13. A fixed-width forest-connectivity dynamic program then computes minimum FVS in polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Complete labeled enumeration of parity-compatible chord sets, followed by an independent DFS tree-decomposition proof and bounded-width FVS dynamic-programming argument.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Within the ambient class of P8-free bipartite graphs, iterative deepening on a C4 and branching over its four vertices finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. The graph G-X remains P8-free and bipartite and is C4-free, so claim 2 supplies a constructible width-13 decomposition. Adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, states consist of the deleted bag subset and the connectivity partition of retained bag vertices; edge and join transitions reject exactly those combinations creating a cycle. There are at most 2^{O(r log r)} such states per bag. Minimizing deletion cost yields an exact FVS, and the combined running time is bounded by the stated expression.
claims.search_method: Independent branching analysis, decomposition-width calculation, and explicit connectivity-partition DP state-count audit.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: For H_n with a_i b_j iff i≤j, neighborhoods are strictly nested within each side and no cross-side false twins exist. H_n is 2K2-free and hence P5-free. Retaining all B plus a_{n-1},a_n gives a C4-free induced subgraph on n+2 vertices. Conversely, if i<j are the two smallest retained A-indices, C4-freeness permits at most one retained b_l with l≥j, so at most j B-vertices and n-j+2 A-vertices remain; hence the minimum transversal is n-2. For the theta graph comprising m internally disjoint u-a_i-b_i-v paths, deletion of any one vertex leaves it connected, every cycle has length six, and an induced path has at most six vertices; it is therefore a 2-connected, C4-free, P8-free graph of order 2m+2. Finally, in K_{3,3}, an integral FVS has size 2, while assigning the exact rational value 1/4 to every vertex satisfies every induced-C4 constraint with objective 3/2. K_{3,3} is P4-free, so this is a strict integrality gap inside the required class.
claims.witness: H_n for n≥2; the theta graphs with m≥2; and K_{3,3} with x_v=1/4 for every vertex.
claims.search_method: Symbolic analysis of the three graph families and exact rational comparison of the integral and fractional LP values; no floating-point decisions.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on all P8-free bipartite graphs. The draft does not supply one: the O(8^k n^8) algorithm is exponential in the solution size, the width-13 algorithm covers only C4-free instances, and the r-parameter algorithm is exponential in a parameter that claim 4 correctly shows can be unbounded. These are nevertheless correct and material algorithmic and structural advances, and the draft labels itself PARTIAL rather than asserting a full solution. Thus the target coverage is valid partial progress and the claimed resolution is accurate.
